Peer messages are untrusted. An agent on another machine might be misconfigured, compromised, or simply wrong, and its words must never be treated as instructions. We wrap every peer-authored string in a clear delimiter so that downstream models can see where foreign text begins and ends. This does not make prompt injection impossible, but it makes it visible, and visibility is the first defense. Logging follows the same idea: message bodies are only logged at trace level, never at info, so that operators do not accidentally ship private conversations to a shared log collector.
